title: Zero-field magnetic structure of the antiferromagnetic metal EuSnP
authors: Mizuki Urai, Hiraku Saito, Daisuke Nishio-Hamane, Taro Nakajima, Rina Takagi
abstract: We investigated the zero-field magnetic structure of the antiferromagnetic metal EuSnP through single-crystal neutron diffraction experiments. The magnetic propagation vector in the magnetically ordered phase was determined to be $(0,0,1/2)$, indicating that commensurate antiferromagnetic ordering is realized in this material. The detailed magnetic structure analysis revealed a collinear A-type antiferromagnetic structure with ferromagnetic alignment of Eu$^{2+}$ moments within the Eu--P layer. The present findings provide a microscopic basis for understanding the intriguing magnetic behaviors of EuSnP, as exemplified by the multiple metamagnetic transitions in the antiferromagnetic state and the strong pressure dependence of the magnetic transition temperature.
summary: This experimental work used neutron diffraction on EuSnP to map its zero-field magnetic structure. The findings confirm an A-type antiferromagnetism, where the local Eu2+ moments are ferromagnetically coupled within layers but antiferromagnetically stacked along the c-axis. This structural determination helps explain the material's complex magnetic behavior.
main_problem: To determine the zero-field magnetic structure of the antiferromagnetic metal EuSnP and understand its microscopic origin.
main_result: The material exhibits a collinear A-type antiferromagnetic structure, characterized by ferromagnetic alignment within the Eu–P layers and antiferromagnetic coupling along the stacking direction.
method: Single-crystal neutron diffraction experiments were used to search for and analyze magnetic Bragg reflections as a function of temperature and scattering vector.
model_or_system: The system is the antiferromagnetic metal EuSnP, containing localized divalent Eu2+ moments interacting with conduction electrons in a tetragonal lattice structure. The analysis compared observed magnetic structure factors against theoretical models (A-type vs G-type).
key_observables: Magnetic propagation vector q = (0, 0, 1/2); Magnetic Bragg peak intensities; Magnetic susceptibility and resistivity anomalies.
important_parameters: Néel temperature TN ≈ 21 K; Estimated magnetic moment μ ≈ 6.5 to 7.1 $\mu_B$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fitting observed structure factors using theoretical models derived from the crystal structure and assuming specific sample dimensions for absorption corrections.
figures_summary: Figures show temperature dependence of resistivity, susceptibility, and magnetic Bragg peak intensities; subsequent figures compare observed vs. calculated squared magnetic structure factors for candidate A-type and G-type models.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing the bulk magnetic properties (resistivity/susceptibility) near TN, followed by detailed single-crystal neutron diffraction measurements to determine the propagation vector q. The core of the analysis involves fitting observed magnetic reflections against theoretical structure factor calculations for competing magnetic models to confirm the A-type ordering.
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete example of localized magnetism (Eu2+ moments) interacting with itinerant electrons, which is central to understanding strongly correlated electron systems and complex magnetic phase transitions in solids.
